problem_summary.summary: Implement an iterator that returns BST values in ascending in-order order.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a BST root at construction. BSTIterator supports boolean hasNext() and int next(); next calls are guaranteed valid.
constraints: At most 10^5 calls to hasNext and next
Follow-up: average O(1) operation time and O(h) memory

brute_force.explanation: Materialize the entire in-order traversal at construction, then advance an array index for each next call.
brute_force.correctness_idea: In-order traversal of a BST lists its values in sorted order. Sequentially returning that list therefore matches the required iterator order.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n) constructor time; O(1) per next and hasNext call.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(n) auxiliary for all stored values and the iterative traversal stack.

optimized.explanation: Keep a stack of the path to the next smallest unvisited node. Initially push the root's left spine; after popping a node, push the left spine of its right subtree.
optimized.correctness_idea: The stack top is the next node in in-order traversal: it is the smallest unvisited node on the current search path. Pushing the right child's left spine schedules exactly the nodes that follow the popped node.
optimized.time_complexity: O(1) amortized per next call because each node is pushed and popped once; O(1) per hasNext.
optimized.space_complexity: O(h) auxiliary for the active root-to-leaf path.

steps.event: Initialize by pushing the left spine.

steps.condition: The right subtree's left spine is just node 6.

steps.action: Return true, then pop and return 6.

edge_cases.handling: The node is pushed and returned once, after which hasNext is false.
The stack may contain O(n) nodes, which is O(h) for this shape.

edge_cases.case: A popped node has a right subtree
edge_cases.handling: Its left spine is pushed before the next call, preserving sorted order.
